title: I Told You So Is Leadership Profanity
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues that 'I told you so,' in any of its many disguised forms, is one of the most corrosive phrases a leader can use, since it makes people feel foolish rather than supported after a mistake. It provides an extensive list of common substitute phrases that carry the same sting despite sounding softer, warning that leaders often say these things unconsciously. The article recommends leaders instead offer support and empathy after a misstep, deliberately withholding any reference to having predicted the outcome correctly.
points: The phrase 'I told you so,' in any form, is described as corrosive to trust and psychological safety.
A long list of disguised equivalents is provided, since leaders often use these unconsciously.
The behavior tends to make people withdraw, get defensive, or stop admitting mistakes openly.
The recommended alternative is offering support and empathy while deliberately not claiming credit for foresight.
quotes: That’s because they know very few leadership phrases invoke as much distaste, disgust, and defensiveness as those four simple words.
Telling others that you knew all along that they would fail or misstep is akin to a slap in the face.
Leaders who use the expression diminish the trust and support necessary for others to admit a mistake or take accountability in the future.
But it is the leader who doesn’t realize they are saying it that creates the most harm.
I told you so” is leadership profanity. Good leaders don’t swear at people when they make an avoidable mistake.
